title: Magnetic coil fixing device and autowinder

features.item: A housing containing a displaceable magnet and pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.
A magnet displaceable along a direction between a gripping position and a release position.
Pole shoes attached to the housing, each with a workpiece contact surface.
Pole shoes designed to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.
A workpiece contact surface defining a contact surface angle of 170° to 190° with the displacement direction.
A magnetic gripper with housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes where contact surface angle is 170° to 190° relative to displacement direction.
A magnetic gripper system with a magnetic gripper and ferromagnetic workpiece, where magnet in gripping position presses workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.
Housing extending along a longitudinal axis with displacement direction parallel to that axis.
Pole shoes with an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
An active structure with a bevel defining a bevel angle of 5° to 85° with the workpiece contact surface.
An active structure with multiple projections for directing magnetic field and forming the workpiece contact surface.
Adjacent first and second projections with a recess between them, recess depth or length deviating by at most 25% from projection length.
A positioning device on the magnetic gripper for positioning the ferromagnetic workpiece on the contact surface.
First and second pole shoes where the magnet in gripping position makes the first pole shoe act as north pole and second as south pole.
A magnet displaceable electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically between gripping and release positions.
A position sensor detecting gripping position and/or release position, or a workpiece sensor detecting the ferromagnetic workpiece.
Housing with a receptacle for receiving a workpiece sensor and/or a supply line.
A manipulator interface on the magnetic gripper for attaching to a manipulator.
Housing portion designed to suppress magnetic field escape, or a shielding device to at least partially prevent magnetic field escape.
At least one projection with length deviating by at most 25% from the thickness of the ferromagnetic workpiece.
A receptacle in the form of a groove in the housing.
A bevel angle of 15° to 75° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
A bevel angle of 40° to 60° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.

claims.note: The reference discloses a magnetic fixing device, which is a type of magnetic gripper, but it is for fixing a magnetic coil to a rotor, not for gripping a ferromagnetic workpiece.
The reference describes a magnetic fixing device but does not disclose a magnet that is displaceable along a displacement direction between a gripping position and a release position.
The reference does not disclose pole shoes attached to a housing, nor does it describe guiding a magnetic field portion to a workpiece contact surface.
The reference does not disclose a workpiece contact surface or a contact surface angle between it and a displacement direction.
This reference describes a magnetic fixing device for a magnetic coil, not a magnetic gripper for a ferromagnetic workpiece, and does not mention contact surface angles or their specific ranges.
This reference describes a magnetic fixing device for a magnetic coil, not a magnetic gripper with a housing that extends along a longitudinal axis.
This reference describes a magnetic fixing device for a magnetic coil, not a magnetic gripper with a displacement direction aligned parallel to a longitudinal axis.
This reference describes a magnetic fixing device for a magnetic coil, not a magnetic gripper with pole shoes having an active structure for directing a magnetic field portion.
This reference describes a magnetic fixing device for a magnetic coil, but does not mention any active structure having a bevel.
This reference describes a magnetic fixing device for a magnetic coil, but does not mention any bevel or workpiece contact surface, or a bevel angle.
This reference describes a magnetic fixing device for a magnetic coil, but does not mention any bevel angle or specific ranges for such an angle.

This reference describes a magnetic fixing device with clip elements, but does not mention an active structure with a plurality of projections for directing a magnetic field or forming a workpiece contact surface.
This reference describes a magnetic fixing device with first and second clip elements, but does not mention projections or a plurality of projections, let alone first and second projections.
This reference does not describe any projections, so it cannot describe first and second projections being adjacent to one another.
This reference does not describe an active structure, projections, or a recess between projections.
This reference does not describe recesses or projections, so it cannot describe their dimensions or relationships.
The reference describes a magnetic fixing device for a magnetic coil, but it does not mention a positioning device for a ferromagnetic workpiece on a workpiece contact surface.
The reference describes a first and second clip element, but not pole shoes.
The reference describes magnetic attachment between clip elements but does not mention pole shoes acting as north and south poles in a gripping position.
The reference describes a magnetic fixing device but does not mention a magnet displaceable electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically between gripping and release positions.
This reference describes a magnetic fixing device for a magnetic coil, but it does not mention a position sensor for detecting gripping or release positions.
This reference describes a magnetic fixing device for a magnetic coil, but it does not mention a workpiece sensor for detecting a ferromagnetic workpiece.
This reference describes a magnetic fixing device, but it does not mention a housing with a receptacle for a workpiece sensor or a supply line.
This reference describes a magnetic fixing device for an autowinder, but it does not mention a manipulator interface for attaching the magnetic gripper to a manipulator.
This reference does not discuss suppressing the escape of a magnetic field from a housing portion.
This reference does not describe a shielding device to prevent magnetic field escape.
This reference describes a magnetic fixing device, not a magnetic gripper system.
This reference describes a magnetic fixing device for a magnetic coil, not a magnetic gripper for a ferromagnetic workpiece.

This reference describes a magnetic fixing device for a magnetic coil, not a magnetic gripper system with a gripping state, gripping position, and a ferromagnetic workpiece pressed against workpiece contact surfaces by magnetic force.

This reference describes a magnetic fixing device for a magnetic coil, not a magnetic gripper system with a release state, release position, and a ferromagnetic workpiece not pressed by magnetic force.
This reference does not describe projections or their length in relation to the thickness of a ferromagnetic workpiece.
This reference does not describe a receptacle in the form of a groove. It describes clip elements for fixing a magnetic coil.

overall.why: The reference describes a magnetic fixing device for a magnetic coil, which is a different application and mechanism than a magnetic gripper with a displaceable magnet and pole shoes for gripping workpieces.
